coverage_note: File ends 33:10 (phone call 29:36-33:06, English). Mostly English explanation of the plural-as-feminine rule; engine-written Latin for his Arabizi at 12:00-29:30. Not filed: 01:53 Amal 'إنت؟' (reads as 'and you?'), 20:33 behkesh->behkish (his own self-fix, then Amal gave the rule), 24:07-24:18 minhek / minhekishitani (likely engine for min ay ishi taani, she accepted), 28:35-29:24 in basatetish vs inbastatish (letter/vowel slip, S4), 21:00 balabesh (dropped 3, S4), 07:24 'At this moment' (English gloss of her phrase). Echo candidates: none Arabic-sounding; only fillers (Um, Uh-huh) and a real 'Biddesh?' repeat of her form (not a slip).

rows.amal_said: No. You're a key. You can't open.
rows.why: He answered 'how is your day' with 'I am open' (maftoo7, sheet: open | Maftoo7); Amal said no; he then found أنا مرتاح (Amal 'Mm-hmm', chat ana mertaa7; sheet: comfortable / relaxed | Mertaa7).

rows.medi_said: شغلت بيتي. من بيتي؟ لا، شغلت بيتي.
rows.why: 'worked my house' lacks min (from); he floated من بيتي as a question, went back to the bare form, and Amal confirmed صح، من بيتي and he repeated it.
'last meeting' needs aa5er + a bare singular noun (sheet: Aa5er + noun); he built el-aakhir + plural-with-my and kept saying اجتماعاتي الأخيرة (04:04); Amal: 'It's one. اجتماع.' then 'Plural.'

rows.amal_said: No، اجتماع is masculine. ... You don't need a t.
rows.why: Feminine adjective (الأخيرة, -a) on masculine singular اجتماع; Amal: 'No، اجتماع is masculine. You don't need a t.' (he reached اجتماعي الأخير at 04:50).

rows.chat: ijtimaa3i el-a5eer / aa5er ijtimaa3 ili kaan 3ala el-wa7de
rows.why: Clock time needs the el- (3ala el-wa7de); Amal answered with الوحدة and he repeated الـ واحدة; 05:11 is a repeat of her fix.

rows.medi_said: خمس، mm-hmm، uh, خمس إحدى عشر،
rows.why: Giving today's date (5th) he said خمس; Amal 'Mm. No.', he fixed 'I mean، خمسة' and she said 'Mm-hmm'. Could be only the engine dropping the final -a (S4); the 'No' also came right after إحدى عشر (MSA 11 vs her e7da3sh).

rows.medi_said: الساعة، uh, تسعة عشر إلا اثني عشر.
rows.why: Time answer reads as 19 minus 12 (24-hour/MSA digits); Amal's chat gave the clock time 'tentain illa tult' and she did not say it aloud. Probably the engine garbling a time such as 'tentain illa tult'; low confidence, chat alone is not a correction.

Temperature 'about 65': he said خمس و ... ستة عشر (sixteen) where sitteen (sixty) was meant; Amal said 'No. مش خمس' at 08:10/08:13 then 'Wow', and typed 5amse u sitteen. Her voiced 'no' was on the خمس start, so which word she rejected is unclear.

rows.medi_said: for باد I can use like بادات.
rows.amal_said: No. مش هيك. For example, الدروس صعبة
rows.why: He tested adding -at to an adjective for a non-human plural; Amal 'No. مش هيك' and gave feminine singular الدروس صعبة. It is a question about the rule, so low confidence.
rows.english: for 'bad' I can add -aat for plural

rows.why: Repeating her example he said a masculine adjective with el- (engine wrote السبع = el-sa3b); Amal 'No. صعبة.'; he answered 'But that's not feminine ... singular feminine'. Needs fem. singular, no el- for a sentence (A7).

rows.amal_said: That's I don't miss. I don't complain.
rows.why: She asked 'I don't complain'; he said bashtesh (= I don't miss, bishta2) and Amal said 'That's I don't miss. I don't complain' (sheet: complain | Eshki | اشتكي); he then tried 'beshtesh'.

rows.amal_said: مهم. Where's the t؟ You keep the t.
rows.why: Negative command 'don't be annoyed' needs the you-form t (ma tenze3jesh); Amal 'Where's the t? You keep the t.' then 'Again', 'بنزعج، صح' (the n), 'لا، t command. Command t.'

rows.medi_said: but, uh, if I do enzaigish, there's no ma, right? Enzaigish.
rows.why: He tried an en- (I/we) form without ma for the command; Amal 'لا، it doesn't work. تنزعجش.' and added ما تنزعجش is also fine.

rows.medi_said: Ma, um, maten, uh, matenbisti. Don't enjoy it. Matenbisti.
rows.proposed_rule: Colloquial negation closes a negated verb with -ish: ma + verb + sh, keeping a long vowel long (ma tenbestish, بحكيش, بمشيش).
rows.why: The -ish at the end of a negated verb was missing; Amal 'No. Where's your ish?' and again at 26:05, he fumbled until 26:37 'Matenbisti ish, fio', which she accepted; chat ma / tenbestish fiyyo zyaade.

'too much' = ziaadeh (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh); he said ziyad (also a man's name) and Amal began 'Zia.' as a prompt; he repeated 'ziyad' and she moved on with 'Where's your ish?', chat has zyaade.
